That's not what he's saying. Obviously, certain metabolic adaptations occur when you subject yourself to an extreme caloric deficit, (or even a moderate one for a long duration). You're consuming less food so your body uses less energy in digestion. NEAT (Non-exercise-activity Thermogenesis) can decrease over time to compensate (this is the subconscious fidgeting you do that can make up a good portion of your caloric expenditure) , and BMR (Basal Metabolic Rate) lowers as an individual's weight drops from being in a deficit.

BUT none of these things invalidate the laws of thermodynamics. Calories In vs. Calories Out still determines whether weight loss occurs. It just may require more effort if an individual goes about dieting in a poor manner (starvation/binge eating leading to yo-yo dieting, etc.).
